poster_title: EvoAgentX: An Automated Framework for Evolving Agentic Workflows
authors: Yingxu Wang, Siwei Liu, Jinyuan Fang, Zaiqiao Meng

panels.headline: Reduce manual efforts and improve scalability of multi-agent systems
content: Multi-agent systems (MAS) are powerful for orchestrating large language models (LLMs) and specialized tools.
Existing MAS frameworks often require manual workflow configuration.
Lack of dynamic evolution and performance optimization mechanisms.
Fragmented toolchains and manual setup hinder consistent application of optimization techniques.
EvoAgentX addresses these limitations through automation and evolution.

panels.headline: Manual workflow configuration limits scalability and adaptability
content: Manual efforts in defining roles, task decomposition, and agent interactions.
Lack of mechanisms for dynamic workflow evolution and optimization.
Inconsistent application of optimization techniques across diverse tasks.
Need for a unified framework to support dynamic and efficient multi-agent workflows.

panels.headline: Modular architecture with five core layers
content: EvoAgentX employs a modular architecture with five core layers: basic components, agent, workflow, evolving, and evaluation.
The evolving layer integrates three optimization algorithms (TextGrad, AFlow, and MIPRO) for iterative refinement.
panels.figure_caption: The framework of EvoAgentX. It illustrates the modular architecture including the basic components, agent, workflow, evolving, and evaluation layers.

panels.headline: Evaluated on diverse benchmarks
content: Evaluated on HotPotQA for multi-hop reasoning, MBPP for code generation, MATH for mathematical problem solving, and GAIA for real-world multi-agent tasks.
Used built-in benchmarks and standardized evaluation metrics for systematic performance assessment.
panels.figure_caption: Statistics of different benchmarks. We denote Question Answering and Natural Questions as QA and NQ, respectively.

panels.headline: Achieved significant performance improvements
content: Achieved a 7.44% increase in HotPotQA F1 score.
Improved MBPP pass@1 by 10.00%.
Gained a 10.00% improvement in MATH solve accuracy.
Overall accuracy on GAIA improved by up to 20.00%.
panels.figure_caption: Performance comparison across different benchmarks. Bold indicates the best performance.

panels.headline: EvoAgentX significantly improves multi-agent system performance
content: EvoAgentX significantly improves the performance of multi-agent systems through dynamic workflow evolution and optimization.
The platform reduces manual efforts and facilitates the rapid development of agent-based applications.
Provides a unified framework for integrating optimization algorithms and benchmarks.
Has the potential to enhance the scalability and adaptability of multi-agent systems in various domains.
Future work may explore generalizability to other tasks and domains.
